question: Five receipts sighted a ~0.157-0.25 ms floor and every one AMORTISED it by batching. Batching requires the work to be known up front; autoregressive decode does not have that. So: is the floor a property of SUBMISSION or of WAITING? The two have opposite consequences.
prediction_written_first: scratchpad/sync_floor_prediction.json -- P1 a graph-expressible serial chain costs ~11us/step not ~157; P2 a host-dependent loop pays the full floor per step, gap 5-8x; P3 therefore the floor argues against HOST-VISIBLE CONTROL FLOW, not against small kernels.
the_finding: THE FLOOR IS WAITING, NOT SUBMITTING. A strictly SERIAL dependency chain -- every step needs the previous -- costs 41.1us per step when MLX can express the dependency in its own lazy graph, against 254.1us when the host blocks each step. Serial does NOT imply per-step sync, and five receipts' worth of 'batch it' was answering a narrower question than it appeared to.
the_sub_finding_that_matters_more_for_de: eval-each (254.1us) and a REAL host-dependent branch (267.4us) are 5.1% apart, INSIDE the noise -- INDISTINGUISHABLE. The data-dependent DECISION is free; the SYNCHRONISATION is the entire cost. So a decode loop is not expensive because it branches, it is expensive because the branch forces a host round trip.

predictions_graded.P1_magnitude: MISSED HIGH -- predicted ~11us/step from the AirGraph within-command-buffer constant, measured 41.1us, 3.7x above. The direction (far below the floor) holds; the constant did NOT reproduce and the contended machine is the obvious candidate, unverified.
predictions_graded.P2: CONFIRMED -- predicted a 5-8x gap, measured 6.19x and 6.51x, both inside the band. This is the FIRST prediction in a long run to land inside rather than above.
predictions_graded.P3: SUPPORTED by P1+P2 holding directionally, and it is a CONSEQUENCE not a measurement.

claim_boundary.noise: ALL THREE ARMS carry 34-39% IQR, far ABOVE this program's 10% gate, because the operator's model-lake fill is deliberately saturating the machine. Admitted ONLY by margin-over-noise: 519% margin against 38.71% worst-arm noise = 13.4x, clearing the 5x hatch. THE DIRECTION IS CERTAIN, THE MAGNITUDES ARE NOT, and no per-step microsecond figure here may be quoted as a measured constant.
claim_boundary.not_reproduced: the ~11us within-command-buffer dispatch cost did NOT reproduce here (41.1us). Either contention or a different code path; not established which.
claim_boundary.scope: one elementwise chain, f32, 16 steps, one machine, INSTANCE. No model executed. This is the SHAPE of a decode dependency, not a decode.
claim_boundary.what_it_does_not_show: it does NOT show the round trip can be removed for a genuinely host-dependent workload -- it shows what that round trip COSTS. Keeping the decision on device (on-GPU sampling, on-GPU routing) is the implied lever and is NOT built or measured here.

tests: no kernel changed, no test count moves, no performance claim about any kernel moves
